⚡ SPI Master Interface

SPI - MASTER INTERFACE SYSTEM

Theme: Serial Communication Interfaces (SPI Master Interface)

Theme: Serial Communication Interfaces (SPI Master Interface)

Our mini project is based on the theme “Serial Communication Interface”. A serial communication interface is a data link that sends information one bit at a time over a small number of lines, using a shared clock and control signals to keep the sender and receiver synchronised. This reduces wiring and makes data exchange between devices reliable and repeatable.

The project focuses on developing a 4-bit SPI-style master/slave interface using standard 74HC logic ICs. A 555 timer generates a 10 kHz clock, and a 74HC393 counter controls the load and shift sequence of one complete transfer, which takes 24 clock cycles. 74HC165 and 74HC595 shift register pairs convert 4-bit DIP switch data to serial form and back to parallel, so the data appears on LEDs at the slave. The system is intended to replace multi-wire parallel transfer with a simple, low-cost, automatic serial link, and it can later be extended to sensor data.

The project combines digital logic design, timing and clock generation, sequential circuit control, shift-register-based data conversion, circuit simulation in Proteus and Logisim, and breadboard implementation with system validation.

INTRODUCTION

• Problem Statement :

Parallel data transfer needs one wire for every bit, so 4 bits take at least 4 data lines plus ground. As the width grows to 8, 16 or 32 bits, the wiring and pin count grow with it. This makes the circuit costly, bulky and hard to route.

• Outcome :

The 4-bit data is transferred using only a few lines (clock, data, load/latch, ground) instead of one wire per bit.

Parallel vs. Serial Data Communication Comparison

Comparison Parameter Parallel Data Transfer SPI Serial Data Transfer (This Design)
Pin / Wire Requirement N signal lines + Ground (4 bits = 5 wires, 32 bits = 33 wires) Fixed 4 lines (MOSI, MISO, SCLK, SH/LD, GND) regardless of data width
PCB Routing Complexity High congestion; multiple parallel traces cause pin routing bottlenecks Low; compact 4-wire serial bus interconnect
Hardware Cost High cable cost, bulky connectors, high pin-count package ICs Low cost, compact discrete IC package, minimal connectors
Signal Crosstalk Significant risk of clock skew and line-to-line crosstalk Clean, synchronous edge-triggered transmission with common ground

DESIGN

Block diagram

Components and their specification

Component Name Part / IC Number Package Type Key Specifications Circuit Function
Parallel-In Serial-Out Shift Register SN74HC165N 16-Pin DIP Supply: 2V - 6V, Asynchronous parallel load, Serial out Q7/Q7\ Captures 4-bit DIP switch data and transmits serially via MOSI/MISO
Serial-In Parallel-Out Shift Register SN74HC595N 16-Pin DIP Storage register with 3-state output latches, 100MHz shift freq Receives serial data and latches directly onto the 4 LEDs flicker-free
Dual 4-Bit Binary Counter SN74HC393N 14-Pin DIP Ripple counter, Negative-edge triggered, 4-stage divide-by-16 Sequences transmission states (Counts 0-7: Shift, Counts 8-15: Load)
Hex Inverter Gate SN74HC04N 14-Pin DIP 6 independent NOT gates, High-speed CMOS Inverts counter bit Q3 to produce active-low SH/LD\ control signal
Clock Timer IC NE555P 8-Pin DIP Astable multivibrator, adjustable duty cycle Generates the 10 kHz base master clock for high-speed transfer
4-Position DIP Switches DIPSW_4 Through-Hole SPST slide switches, 2.54mm pitch Provides manual parallel 4-bit digital input data (0000 to 1111)
